paragraphs.source_en: “The concept of emptiness and stillness is cherished by practitioners of the Way of Tea and held up as a constant admonition to themselves. Yet worldly people merely assume the outward appearance of emptiness and stillness, while possessing none of its substance within. A tea gathering that bears only its outward guise, squanders vast sums, and flaunts rare treasures—such affected elegance in the name of emptiness is better done without.”

paragraphs.source_en: On the first day of the ninth month of Tenshō 18, Hideyoshi returned triumphantly to the capital. Gazing at the long procession of courtiers who had come to welcome him at Yamashina, he turned to Ishida Mitsunari and said, “Jibu, at last we are back in the capital.” Although Hideyoshi's attire that day was no less extraordinary than it had been at his departure, no one now found it comical or strange. Hideyoshi's style had come to rule the age completely.
